local_checks.invariant: Contributor-controlled code (fork PR, Dependabot PR) never runs with secrets, a write token, or publish authority.
local_checks.result: Triggers are push to hardened, pull_request (not pull_request_target) and workflow_dispatch (ci.yml:6-10). Workflow-level permissions are contents: read (ci.yml:12-13) and no job widens them. No secrets.* reference, no environment, no registry login, no push: the image job builds with no push (ci.yml:64-65) and the only artifact is the SBOM upload (ci.yml:113-117). Every checkout sets persist-credentials: false (ci.yml:30-31,48-49,62-63,93-94,106-107). No ${{ github.event.* }} value is interpolated into a run step; only matrix.node goes into a with: input (ci.yml:34). Fork PR jobs therefore run contributor code only on an ephemeral runner with a read-only token and nothing to publish.

local_checks.invariant: Third-party actions and CI tool images are bound to immutable identities, and no PR-writable cache feeds a trusted job.
local_checks.result: actions/checkout, actions/setup-node and actions/upload-artifact are pinned by 40-hex commit SHA (ci.yml:30,32,113); the gitleaks image is pinned by sha256 digest (ci.yml:53). The setup-node npm cache (ci.yml:35-36) is keyed on the lockfile; GitHub scopes caches written by pull_request runs to the PR merge ref, so a fork cannot seed the cache read by the push job on hardened, and npm ci verifies each tarball against the lockfile integrity anyway.

local_checks.invariant: Dependency resolution for tests and the image is lockfile-bound with integrity and runs no install scripts.
local_checks.result: package.json pins exact versions (package.json:18-27). package-lock.json is lockfileVersion 3 with 131 entries; every non-root entry resolves to https://registry.npmjs.org/ and carries an integrity hash, and no entry has hasInstallScript (parsed with python3 -I json over the file). Every npm ci runs with --ignore-scripts (ci.yml:37,100,110; Dockerfile:8).

local_checks.invariant: Only intended release inputs enter the image; no secret, override, allowlist, state or fixture reaches the build context.
local_checks.result: .dockerignore is a deny-all allowlist (.dockerignore:2) that re-admits only haval-h6-mqtt/package.json, package-lock.json and top-level *.js (.dockerignore:3-5). secrets/, docker-compose.override.yml, proxy/allowlist.local.txt, data/, test/ and node_modules/ are therefore excluded. local_checks.invariant: PR-controlled container images or shell interpolation in CI cannot reach a trusted job or credential.
local_checks.result: The image job runs scripts/init-secrets.sh (ci.yml:85), which docker-runs the image named by the checked-out docker-compose.yml (scripts/init-secrets.sh:34,37), and the integration job runs test/integration/run.sh (ci.yml:101), which interpolates container output into bash -c checks (test/integration/run.sh:68,83-85). In a fork PR all of these inputs are already contributor-controlled code in the same secret-less, contents:read, non-publishing job; on push to hardened they are reviewed repository content. local_checks.invariant: Automated update and developer-hook paths do not merge or execute unreviewed code with elevated authority.
local_checks.result: Dependabot only opens weekly PRs for npm, docker, docker-compose and github-actions (.github/dependabot.yml:4-20); the repository has no auto-merge workflow, and Dependabot PRs run the same pull_request workflow with a read-only token. The pre-commit gitleaks hook uses the mutable tag rev v8.28.0 (.pre-commit-config.yaml:3-4); it runs only on a developer workstation and the tag writer is the same gitleaks maintainer set that authors the pinned code, so no new trust is added (recorded as hardening).

hardening_notes: The sbom job runs npx --yes @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm@6.0.1 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:112): the tool version is pinned but its transitive dependency tree resolves at run time without a lockfile. local_checks.invariant: Every outbound login passes LoginLimiter.tryAcquire, and the 3-per-rolling-hour cap is persisted before the request is sent and cannot be raced
local_checks.result: The only login path is GwmClient.login (carConnector.js:162-192). It calls limiter.tryAcquire() first (carConnector.js:163). authed() reaches it only at carConnector.js:207 and 214. tryAcquire is synchronous: it prunes, checks, pushes and calls store.update before it returns (backoff.js:54-63). Concurrent callers therefore cannot pass the check together. If store.update throws (data dir unwritable), login throws before any HTTP request, so the cap fails closed. login_capped carries retryAfterMs, and reader.onFailure honours it (reader.js:184, 260). No path sends a login outside the cap.

local_checks.invariant: Three consecutive authentication failures halt polling, the halt is persisted, and only the owner clears it
local_checks.result: Auth-flagged GwmErrors come from parse on 401/403 or AUTH_CODES (carConnector.js:155,158) and from any non-SUCCESS login except BUSY_CODES (carConnector.js:175-178). They increment reader.authFailures on both timers (reader.js:178, 252-253). The counter resets only after a full successful status cycle (reader.js:161). At 3 failures, halt() sets stopped, clears the timers and persists halted (reader.js:190-201). start() refuses to poll while halted is set (reader.js:84-90). Only the owner CLI --reset-halt clears it (index.js:19-24). authFailures is in memory, but the persisted login cap bounds a crash-restart loop to 3 logins per hour. Rate-limit, busy and login_capped errors do not count toward the halt by design. No lower-trust principal can write /data (reader-data volume, store.js atomic tmp+rename, store.js:389-398).

local_checks.invariant: Bounded local check of the cap under concurrency, a corrupt state file and a backward clock step
local_checks.result: Sandbox harness (no network, dummy data, fake transport). (A) Two concurrent authed() calls without a usable token sent 2 logins (no single-flight), then a third login succeeded and a fourth failed with login_capped: the cap held at 3. (B) With 3 recent attempts and halted persisted, tryAcquire returned ok=false. After state.json was overwritten with invalid JSON, Store logged 'state file unreadable; starting empty', halted became null and tryAcquire returned ok=true: the store fails open. (C) With 3 persisted attempts and the clock moved back 120 s, tryAcquire returned ok=true because prune drops a > t (backoff.js:51). B and C need owner or host control of /data or the clock, so they are hardening, not findings.

hardening_notes: Fixture-mode credential egress (config.js:49, carConnector.js:170-172; local check-1 D): any two non-gwmcloud URLs select fixture mode without GWM_LIVE_ENABLED. loadConfig still loads the real /run/secrets credentials, and login sends the account and the MD5 password over plain http if the URLs say so. The MD5 alone is enough to sign in. A mistyped or migrated GWM domain silently bypasses the live gate. Fix: require an explicit GWM_FIXTURE=true. In fixture mode, refuse to start when /run/secrets/gwm_* are the defaults, or require https. Regression test: liveGate with two non-gwmcloud URLs and no fixture flag returns run:false.

No single-flight login (carConnector.js:206-222; local check-1 A): the status and charge timers that call authed() together each log in, so one renewal uses 2 slots of the 3-per-hour cap. README says that two sign-ins sign each other out, so this can create self-inflicted auth failures toward the halt. Fix: memoize the in-flight login promise in GwmClient and reuse it, so that concurrent authed() calls perform exactly one login.

Store.load fails open (store.js:24-31; local check-1 B): when state.json is unreadable, the store starts empty and silently clears the persisted halt flag and the login-cap history. Fix: on a non-ENOENT read or parse error, exit with EX_CONFIG, or treat the cap as exhausted for one window and keep halted=true until the owner runs --reset-halt.

LoginLimiter.prune drops future-dated attempts (backoff.js:51; local check-1 C): a backward clock step resets the persisted cap. Fix: clamp entries with a > t to t, so they still count for the window.

MQTT_URL is not validated (config.js:174): mqtt://user:pass@host bypasses the file-only secret rule. The MQTT password is also never passed to registerSecret (index.js:65, config.js:133). Fix: parse MQTT_URL, refuse userinfo, and call registerSecret(config.mqttPassword) at startup.

unregisterSecret on token rotation (carConnector.js:134-135, 179-180) removes old tokens from the redactor. The secret Set has no reference count, so a collision with another registered value also unregisters that value. Opaque (non-JWT) old tokens would then log in clear. Fix: keep rotated tokens registered for the process lifetime.

first-run.sh report section 1 drops the Squid client address field (first-run.sh:39 prints $3,$5; squid.conf:26 puts %>a in $2). CONNECTs from any container on mqtt_internal (HA, others) look like reader attempts during the allowlist review. Fix: print $2 too, or filter on the gwm-reader container IP.

derive-dashboard.js denylist (derive-dashboard.js:20) does not cover toggle, url or fire-dom-event actions, or hass.callService inside custom:button-card [[[ ]]] templates. Fix: switch to an allowlist of action types (more-info, navigate, none), and reject templates that reference hass.call*.

test/integration/run.sh:83-88 interpolates netprobe JSON values into bash -c. This is safe today because the values are Node constants or integers. Fix: pass them as positional arguments (bash -c '...' _ "$v"), as run.sh:112 already does.

init-secrets.sh:32 makes gwm_username and gwm_password mode 0644. Their confidentiality on the host depends only on secrets/ staying 0700 (init-secrets.sh:12-14). Document this, or use a group-readable 0640 with the container gid.

local_checks.invariant: The untrusted GWM charge-log response must have an effective size/cardinality bound before it is buffered and republished.
local_checks.result: The transport caps every response body. httpClient.js:21 sets MAX_BODY_BYTES = 4*1024*1024 and lines 143-150 destroy the request with a GwmError once cumulative response bytes exceed 4 MiB. getChargeLogs (carConnector.js:262-270) sends pageNum/pageSize=100 but returns data.list verbatim with no length or per-item cap, so list cardinality is not self-limited; it is instead bounded by the 4 MiB raw-body cap (about 10^5 minimal {startTime,endTime} entries). routes.js:45-59 confirms the POST /vehicleCharge/getChargeLogs path is reachable (allowlisted) with a pinned body, so the path is live. An effective upstream bound exists; the input-to-buffer path is not unbounded.

local_checks.invariant: The MQTT outgoing store must not accumulate without bound when the broker is slow, offline, or the charge list is large.
local_checks.result: pollCharge (reader.js:241-250) formats the bounded list and publishes it as ONE retained QoS1 attribute message (gwmbrasil/<id>/charging_history/attributes), not one message per entry, so a single poll adds one message of a few MiB at most. The poll loop is strictly sequential: scheduleCharge/scheduleStatus (reader.js:107-123) schedule the next cycle only after the prior async cycle resolves, and each publish is awaited. mqtt 5.16.0 (package-lock.json:12) stores QoS1 packets when disconnected (node_modules/mqtt build/lib/client.js:1122-1128 -> _storePacket) and resolves the reader's publish promise only on PUBACK (outgoing[messageId].cb). Therefore an unreachable broker STALLS the awaiting cycle instead of spinning and accumulating per-cycle; in-flight/outgoing state is bounded to a single cycle. No unbounded buffering across cycles.

hardening_notes: haval-h6-mqtt/carConnector.js:262-270 getChargeLogs returns data.list verbatim; add a reader-side list.slice(0, 100) (the pageSize:"100" at :266 is only a request hint the server may ignore) so the retained charging_history attribute size does not depend on the server honoring the page size.

haval-h6-mqtt/reader.js:56-58 formatChargeLogs constructs four Intl date/time formatters per charge entry; linear with a large constant and self-limited to the reader's own 0.5 cpu, so hardening not a finding - hoist the formatters out of the map callback.

mosquitto/mosquitto.conf omits max_connections, max_queued_messages, memory_limit and message_size_limit; add explicit values (message_size_limit sized just above the ~6 MiB retained charge payload - the 4 MiB input body expands ~1.4x through formatChargeLogs) as defense-in-depth against a compromised or credential-leaked peer on mqtt_internal, since the container memory cap is 64m.
proxy/squid.conf omits client_lifetime and per-client maxconn; add them to bound long-lived or many CONNECT tunnels from an internal peer, complementing the 128m container memory cap.

haval-h6-mqtt/mqtt.js:138-151 publish() sets no per-message timeout, so an awaited QoS1 publish promise pends for the entire broker outage; reliability hardening (trigger is broker unavailability, not lower-trust input, so not a finding) - add a publish deadline or a bounded pending-publish count.

hardening_notes: Fixture-mode credential egress (config.js:49, carConnector.js:170-172; local check-1 D): any two non-gwmcloud URLs select fixture mode without GWM_LIVE_ENABLED. loadConfig still loads the real /run/secrets credentials, and login sends the account and the MD5 password over plain http if the URLs say so. No single-flight login (carConnector.js:206-222; local check-1 A): the status and charge timers that call authed() together each log in, so one renewal uses 2 slots of the 3-per-hour cap. Fix: memoize the in-flight login promise in GwmClient and reuse it, so that concurrent authed() calls perform exactly one login.

Store.load fails open (store.js:24-31; local check-1 B): when state.json is unreadable, the store starts empty and silently clears the persisted halt flag and the login-cap history. Fix: on a non-ENOENT read or parse error, exit with EX_CONFIG, or treat the cap as exhausted for one window and keep halted=true until the owner runs --reset-halt.

LoginLimiter.prune drops future-dated attempts (backoff.js:51; local check-1 C): a backward clock step resets the persisted cap. Fix: clamp entries with a > t to t, so they still count for the window.

MQTT_URL is not validated (config.js:174): mqtt://user:pass@host bypasses the file-only secret rule. The MQTT password is also never passed to registerSecret (index.js:65, config.js:133). Fix: parse MQTT_URL, refuse userinfo, and call registerSecret(config.mqttPassword) at startup.

unregisterSecret on token rotation (carConnector.js:134-135, 179-180) removes old tokens from the redactor.
